turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi, this is Elena! Thanks for calling back so fast.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hi Elena, Arjun from HyperSale. Mind if I ask how you ramp new SDRs, so I can tailor the demo?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sure! We onboard four to six new SDRs each quarter, and I run the training myself with role-plays and practice calls. I can’t listen to every call, so reps are often still nervous when they start cold calling, and I don’t have a clear way to show leadership whether the training is working.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That makes sense. How many weeks until a new SDR is call-ready, and how many hours do you spend coaching each cohort?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Usually it takes about three to four weeks before they’re comfortable calling, and I spend roughly eight to ten hours a week coaching each cohort. Can I see how individual reps are improving over time?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Yes—managers see each rep’s week-by-week score trends, and every score links to the exact quote behind it. Which behaviors does leadership most want tracked?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Oh, interesting. Leadership mainly wants to track confidence in the opener, objection handling, discovery questions, and whether reps are consistently using our messaging. How long does setup typically take?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Typically, we can set up one team in three to five business days using your messaging and scenarios. What should reps practise first?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That makes sense. I’d start with cold-call openers and our most common objections, especially around pricing, timing, and prospects already using another logistics provider. Those are the areas where new reps tend to lose confidence fastest.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: When reps lose confidence on those objections, how does that affect ramp time or meetings booked in their first month?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It usually adds about a week to ramp because I have to repeat role-plays and give extra one-on-one coaching. In their first month, they hesitate or end calls too quickly, so they book noticeably fewer meetings than reps who handle those objections confidently.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Roughly how many fewer meetings does each new SDR book in month one, and what would getting that week back mean for your team?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I’d estimate each new SDR books two to three fewer meetings in that first month. Getting that week back would mean faster pipeline contribution, fewer extra coaching hours for me, and a clearer impact I could show leadership.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s 8 to 18 missed meetings per cohort. Would Tuesday at 2 your time work for a demo with you and your SDR manager?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Tuesday at 2 my time works, and I’ll invite our SDR manager as well. Great, talk soon!
